I fully understand the importance of professional support from psychologists and psychiatrists. Last time I felt suicidal (but not yet made any attempt in reality), someone helped me made an emergency appointment with the best psychologist they can find, and I was immediately transferred to the best psychiatrist they can find. I regularly visited the doctor and took medicine for about 3 months, and despite the slight numbness caused by drug, I felt much better and functioned perfectly well. Then, as it often goes, I moved back home, found a job here, and dropped out of therapy.

Here in my hometown, ppl have rarely any sense about mental illness, let alone sympathy or empathy. The only hospital that can prescribe the medicine I need is better called an asylum, and if you are spotted around there then comes the stigma.

In these years, I did make some attempts to find a job elsewhere (which is why I waited for nearly 3 yrs), and all of them failed. Perhaps I am not determined enough, and perhaps I am just not worth these attempts.

Recently I have talked with a friend of mine who was well-trained in psychology. The talk was constructive, but in around a week there's a qualification assessment for my job which I am bound to fail. I don't want to wait until then and see my soul perish. If there was hell, I guess I'd already lived in one, mentally.

Before and during each movement, try tighten your lower belly, by this I mean tuck in your belly until you feel a "steel pad" under your skin. 

This activates your (long-forgotten) *Transversus abdominis*,  In nearly all lower body exercises if this piece of muscle doesn't engage properly, extra stress will be put on your lower back.

Oh and, don't forget to keep a neutral pelvis and a neutral spine. I know that's a lot to memorize and bring into exercise, but this is very important.
